title: 3D Home Building
desc: Understand how large-scale 3D printing of walls and homes works, its safety, codes, costs and where it suits.
outcomes: Explain how a construction printer builds walls.
Write a feasibility note for a small building.
task: Write a feasibility note for a small printed building with design, quantities, time, cost, code checks and risks.
condition: A computer, public information, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor builder. No printer operation is done.
standard: Quantities and time are calculated; code and permit checks are listed; risks and controls are stated; cost compared with conventional building; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Builders, architects in training, housing groups, students.
evidence: quantity sheet, cost comparison, risk list, note
modules: A gantry or arm prints a cement-like mix in layers.
Walls are printed; roofs and services are added by hand.
A design file controls the path.
A printer lays a 40 mm bead in a double-wall pattern.
Cement mixes with additives; earth mixes; recycled aggregates.
Must flow, hold shape and cure.
A hot day needs a retarder.
Structural design by an engineer; reinforcement and openings.
Steel bars are placed in wall cavities.
Wall length x height / layer height = layers.
60 m of wall at 3 m high needs 150 layers of 20 mm.
A fence marks the print zone.
Labour saving vs machine and material cost.
Walls cost 12% less but doors cost the same.
A cube fails; the batch is rejected.
The note recommends a small pilot hut.
quiz: In layers by a gantry or arm.
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: construction and built environment, 3D printing, green building.
local: Building codes and permits differ by place.
ladder: L6: learner can lead a crew.
